content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has warned consumers not to buy or serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars, after receiving several reports of infants choking on the product.

The warning covers all flavors, quantities, lots and dates of the bars. The reports describe infants ages 1.5 to 2.5 years suffering complete airway obstruction, with an inability to breathe, after consuming the product.

The FDA has informed the firm of the adverse event reports and has recommended that the firm recall the product. Consumers should not buy or serve any flavor of the bars and should immediately throw them away, according to the warning.

Separately, a nationwide recall of 365 Whole Foods Market ashwagandha capsules was updated October 30. Vitality Works is recalling one lot — 2025-26227, expiration 10/13/2028 — of 120-count bottles of 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha, because it may contain Salmonella. The capsules were sold at Whole Foods Market stores nationwide and through Amazon from November 24, 2025, through October 20, 2026. Customers should discard capsules from the recalled lot, not return them to the store; refunds are available at any Whole Foods Market store. No illnesses had been reported when the notice was issued, and the potential contamination was identified through routine sampling of a single retail unit.

This story reports the agencies' warnings; it is not medical advice. Consumers with questions about either product can contact the companies or the FDA.

What to watch

Both alerts landed in the same week as the holiday shopping season begins, when snack and supplement purchases spike. The toddler-bar warning is the more urgent of the two: unlike a lot-specific recall, it covers every unit of the product on shelves.

title: FDA warns parents: do not buy or serve Once Upon a Farm toddler snack bars after infant choking reports
